title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

The current generation, continuing the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming. Key model IDs as of mid-2025:

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest Claude 4 |
| Sonnet 4.5 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | Balanced |
| Sonnet 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Current default Sonnet |
| Opus 4.7 | `claude-opus-4-7` | Most capable; also powers Claude Code Fast mode |

Claude 4 models show substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision.

*Note: the table above reflects the lineup as of mid-2025. See the 2026 updates below for the current default models.*

---

## Claude Opus 4.7 (April 2026)

Landed as the new default model on Max and Team Premium plans. Introduced a new **`xhigh` effort level** — recommended for most coding work — along with an interactive `/effort` slider in Claude Code to dial reasoning effort up or down per task.

---

## Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026)

Anthropic's flagship model, priced the same as Opus 4.7 (**$5/$25 per MTok**, $10/$50 in Fast mode). Became the default model for Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and Anthropic API accounts, running at high reasoning effort by default.

On the Super-Agent benchmark, Opus 4.8 is the only model to complete every case end-to-end, and it scored **84% on Online-Mind2Web** — the strongest computer-use/browser-agent result of any model tested, ahead of both Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5. Early testers report it is roughly four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flawed code pass unremarked.

**Key specs:** 1M-token context window by default on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, and Vertex AI (200K on Microsoft Foundry); 128K max output tokens. Also shipped Claude Code's **dynamic workflows** feature — a script Claude writes to orchestrate dozens to hundreds of subagents on large-scale problems.

---

## Claude Sonnet 5 (July 2026)

Billed as the "most agentic Sonnet yet," closing much of the performance gap with Opus 4.8 on reasoning, tool use, coding, and knowledge work while staying priced well below it. Launched at introductory pricing of **$2/$10 per MTok** through August 31, 2026 (reverting to the standard $3/$15 afterward) — versus Opus 4.8's $5/$25.

Matches Opus 4.8's **1M-token context window** and **128K max output tokens**. Uses an updated tokenizer: the same input now maps to roughly **1.0-1.35x more tokens** than under Sonnet 4.6, depending on content type, with the introductory pricing set to keep the switch close to cost-neutral during the discount window.

Sonnet 5 is the default model for Free and Pro plan users, and is also available to Max, Team, and Enterprise users via the API and Claude Code.

---

## Claude Fable 5 (restored July 1, 2026)

Anthropic's Fable model line returned to global availability on July 1, 2026, after the U.S. government lifted an export control order that had restricted access to it.

**Current model IDs (as of July 2026):** `claude-fable-5` (Fable 5), `claude-opus-4-8` (Opus 4.8), `claude-sonnet-5` (Sonnet 5), `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` (Haiku 4.5).

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K tokens (stable since Claude 2.1) → **1M tokens** (Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5, 2026)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use (now a core benchmark target, not just a beta feature)
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus)
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing — Sonnet 5 explicitly closes the gap with Opus 4.8 at roughly 40% of the price
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, and integration with external systems; Claude Code's "dynamic workflows" (2026) push this to scripted orchestration of dozens-to-hundreds of subagents
- **Effort control:** Reasoning effort became a user-tunable dial in 2026 (`xhigh` effort level, `/effort` slider) rather than a fixed per-model setting
